title: Claude produces a computer-checked formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem
friendlyTitle: Claude turned a famous proof into code a computer can check
summary: Anthropic says a multi-agent Claude system completed the first end-to-end Lean formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 11 days. The 13-million-line result uses 29,500 intermediate theorems and was checked by Lean, with outside mathematician Kevin Buzzard reviewing the proof’s structure.
friendlySummary: Claude agents spent 11 days writing Fermat’s Last Theorem in the Lean proof language. Lean then checked each logical step, and an outside mathematician reviewed the result.
whyItMatters: The achievement is about verification rather than discovering a new proof, but that distinction is valuable. Computer-checked formalization could help reviewers validate increasingly large bodies of human- and AI-generated mathematics while preserving a traceable standard of correctness.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI may create more mathematics than people can review by hand. Computer-checked proofs can help people find errors and trust correct results.
